chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Fred Robbins and Latin music on radio
summary: Disc jockey Fred Robbins played the instrumental "Killer Joe" because he could not play Spanish vocals to his jazz audience.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Ah - ha. Okay, well, the one under the Rene Hernandez name, which has a little salsa in it, is very very nice. I understand that is one of the few recordings that Fred Robbins ever played. I understand Fred Robbins played a few Machito recordings on his end and "Killer Joe" was one of them. Did you ever hear "Killer Joe" over the Fred Robbins Show?
Well, yes, I used to listen to Fred Robbins because he always had a good musical program.
Yeah, but I understand he never played much Latin American music except when it came to your band, then he played your stuff.
Well, because in those days there was a lot of singing in Spanish and this one was just ..... .

.....instrumental, so he had a chance. He was a very good friend on my band list, there was no question. He was a good friend of mine or he is a good friend of mine, and he like latin music, but you know, he was Jazz-oriented. He just can't play over the radio somebody singing in Spanish. He lose his audience.....
.... so that particular number give him the chance to play over the radio.
